pages.text: Dingding, a little pig in a crimson apron, pushed the seasoned greens to the edge of the bowl. Only white rice remained in the middle. The bowls for their work break sat on the bank.
"Let's eat and go collect pond snails," Mom said. She worked several paddies on her own. She offered Dingding some greens, but Dingding shook their head and pushed them away.
At the next day's break, the basket felt heavy. Dingding's arms drooped. Even climbing up one paddy level was hard.
Grandma, who had farmed rice all her life, arranged bowls of greens, rice, beans, and soup in a circle on a flat stone. "Let's play the Around the Bowls game."

She pointed out where each food came from: greens from the bank, rice from the paddy, beans from the vegetable patch behind the house, and broth made with water from the valley spring. Dingding stared in wonder.
"Take a bite from every bowl. Don't leave any out!" Grandma sang, "Around the Bowls—Yum, Yum!"
Dingding closed their eyes and tasted the nutty greens. Then came rice, beans, and a sip of soup. "Around the Bowls—Yum, Yum!"
After one full circle, Dingding's arms felt stronger. The greens smelled like the grass on the bank. Dingding lifted the basket.
The next day, Dingding arranged the bowls first. "One, put the bowls in a circle. Two, take a bite from each. Three, finish the whole circle!" Grandma smiled.
Grandma stroked Dingding's back. "A trip around the bowls gives you strength." Dingding ate a little of everything and led the way with the basket. "Around the Bowls—Yum, Yum!"
